question: A colleague proposes running every request on two different tiers and comparing the two answers each time. What is the most reasonable assessment?
options: A) It is wasteful, because the two tiers will always return answers that are effectively identical.
B) It is sensible, because using two tiers spreads consumption across two separate allowances.
C) It is wasteful, since it doubles the allowance spent on a comparison worth doing only once.
D) It is sensible, since comparing two answers each time is the surest way to catch any error.
correct_answers: C) It is wasteful, since it doubles the allowance spent on a comparison worth doing only once.
explanations: Incorrect. They genuinely differ on demanding work, so the objection is cost rather than a lack of difference.
Incorrect. Usage is measured across all of a person's activity, so nothing is spread by using two tiers.
Correct. Comparing tiers is worth doing on a representative sample to settle the choice; repeating it on every request pays twice for a decision already made.
Incorrect. Two answers that agree can both be wrong, so this buys far less assurance than it costs.
